description: The supplied image contains no scientific figure. It is a single, square publisher badge of the kind inserted automatically by journal production systems: on a plain light-grey-to-white background sits a circular ring drawn in two colours — an upper blue arc and a yellow lower/right arc — with an open gap, evoking a refresh/rotation arrow. Centred inside the ring is a solid red shape resembling a ribbon or bookmark, whose lower edge is notched (swallow-tail). Directly beneath the ring, two lines of dark-grey sans-serif text read "Check for" and "updates". This is the "Check for updates" / Crossref-style article-update badge that signals a published paper has an updated version; it carries no axes, no scale bar, no sample label, no composition, no processing condition and no measured value. It is therefore not evidence about the microstructure or deformation behaviour of the Fe-Mn-Al-C austenitic low-density steels described in the paper. Nothing in this image can be linked to any other panel, and no quantitative extraction is possible from it.

observations.observation: The only image supplied for this figure group is a square publisher logo/badge, not a data plot, micrograph, spectrum, map, table or photograph.
The badge consists of a circular ring made of a blue arc and a yellow arc with an open gap, surrounding a solid red ribbon/bookmark shape with a notched lower edge.
Two lines of dark-grey sans-serif text beneath the ring read exactly 'Check for' and 'updates'.
The image contains no axes, tick labels, units, legend, scale bar, colour scale or data labels of any kind.

No sample label, alloy composition, processing condition or measured value appears anywhere in this image, so it cannot be tied to the Fe-28Mn-9Al-0.9C, Fe-28Mn-9Al-5Ni-0.9C or Fe-15Mn-9Al grades discussed in the paper.
No caption was extracted for this figure group, so there is no textual description that could be checked against the pixels.
